description: Twenty grounded-RAG probes for the public (Wikipedia-scale) library. Use with library=public. Coverage depends on indexed shards — empty answers are valid signals to widen Top K or grow the corpus.

cases.query: Summarize what the indexed articles say about any historical event, person, or place they mention. Cite **Article title** for each claim.
cases.note: Corpus-agnostic sanity: forces citation discipline on whatever is in the index.

cases.query: What scientific or technical concepts appear in the retrieved passages? List each with one sentence of support and **Article title**.
cases.note: Tests extraction without assuming a specific topic exists in your slice.

cases.query: Compare how two or more indexed articles describe a shared theme (e.g. geography, biology, technology). Use a markdown table: Theme | **Article title** | Supported detail | Limitation.
cases.note: Compare + optional FLARE stresses multi-doc recall.

cases.query: List any dates, years, or time periods stated in the excerpts and what they refer to. Each bullet must include **Article title**.
cases.note: Temporal grounding — catches hallucinated timelines if model drifts.

cases.query: What datasets, benchmarks, or corpora are named in the retrieved text? If none, say so explicitly.
If the passages describe a process, algorithm, or workflow, outline the steps as a checklist. Otherwise state that the excerpts do not describe a process. Cite **Article title**.
What geographical locations (cities, countries, regions, rivers) are mentioned in the context? Bullet list with **Article title** per location cluster.
What organizations, institutions, or companies appear in the excerpts? One line each with **Article title**.
Do any passages disagree or present alternative viewpoints on the same topic? If so, summarize neutrally with **Article title**. If not, say the excerpts align or are unrelated.
Extract any numerical facts (measurements, populations, years, distances) from the context only. Table: Value | What it refers to | **Article title**.
What biographical facts about any person named in the excerpts can you state? If no person appears, say so. Cite **Article title**.
What causes, effects, or mechanisms are described in the passages? Use ### Causes and ### Effects only if the text supports them; otherwise one short section on limits.
What cultural, artistic, or literary topics appear? Summarize only from excerpts with **Article title**.
What sports, games, or competitions are mentioned? If none, state that clearly.
What medical, biological, or health-related terms appear? Define only using passage wording; cite **Article title**.
What legal, political, or governmental concepts are discussed in the retrieved chunks? Bullet list with **Article title**.
What technologies (software, hardware, networks, energy) are referenced? Compare two if possible; else single-article depth.
In one paragraph, answer: What is the single most concrete fact the union of these excerpts best supports, and why is it well-supported? Name **Article title**.
cases.note: Calibration question for confidence vs evidence.

cases.query: What questions CANNOT be answered from these excerpts alone? List 3–6 gaps as bullets.

Pretend you are briefing a VP in 120 words: what does this slice of the public index contain thematically, and what should they not conclude? Every sentence needs **Article title** anchor where factual.
cases.note: Executive summary + FLARE for possible follow-up retrieval.
